description: Network of Mixtec-speaking city-states and small kingdoms (señoríos) across the Mixteca region of present-day Oaxaca, ascendant after the contraction of Monte Albán and famous for codex-based historical record-keeping, fine metalwork, and the legendary career of the eleventh-century warlord Eight Deer Jaguar Claw. Several Mixtec polities fell tributary to the Mexica in the late fifteenth century without losing internal political organisation.

temporal.notes: Postclassic Mixtec city-states and small kingdoms across the Mixteca region; some annexed by the Mexica in the late fifteenth century but retained local political identity to Spanish contact.

geographic.notes: Centroid set in the Mixteca Alta highlands; political authority was distributed across many small señoríos rather than concentrated at a single capital.
